_comment: Held-out validation grid. Same generator and SAME standardised schema as gen.json -- identical physics/freestream specs, the same save_t_spec drawn per context and written into params.json, and a frame COUNT rather than an iteration cap. That matters most here: a validation corpus at one fixed interval measures a single corner of the dt axis and its scores are not comparable with training, which is the exact failure hfm/data.py's val_fraction note describes. Smaller grid than gen.json on purpose.
_save_t_note: Drawn once per CONTEXT (so params.json is identical down a grid column and the column still groups into one system) and written into params.json. A single fixed interval would give the dt probe a constant target -- hfm/data.py warns 'constant -- dt probe target is degenerate' -- and, because it is the presence of save_t in params.json that flips a run from 'legacy' to 'has_save_t' in the loader, a corpus without it trains under stride augmentation on an inferred dt instead of stride 1 on a recorded one.
_steps_note: Frames per run, mirroring gen_alternating's steps_per_segment: end_t = steps_per_run * save_t, so every run yields exactly steps_per_run + 1 frames whatever its interval. The old n_iter cap made run length depend on the adaptive step, i.e. on the physics draw, so viscous runs came out shorter than inviscid ones.
_problem_note: ELLIPSE ONLY, on purpose: the nozzle mesh generator fails to close its boundary loop (gmsh 'closed loop' error, on Mac AND the cluster), so no nozzle run ever reached the training data — it is 100% ellipse. Matching that means ellipse only; adding nozzle would make validation mismatch the real training distribution and abort on the bad mesh.
